title: Your outdoor country wedding: a simple rain and weather plan
description: Worried about rain at your outdoor country wedding? A local wedding videographer on planning for weather, why rain is not the enemy on film, and timing for light.
seo_title: Your Outdoor Country Wedding: A Simple Rain & Weather Plan — Jack Albert Weddings
body:
If you are getting married outdoors in the country, the one thing that keeps couples up at night is the weather. I understand it. But in all my years filming outdoor weddings in the Ottawa Valley, I can tell you the weather has never actually ruined a day. Here is how to plan so it does not ruin yours, or your film.

Have a plan B, and decide it early

The couples who stay calm are the ones who already have a backup: a tent, a barn, a covered porch, or an indoor space. Decide in advance who makes the rain call and by what time. Once that is settled, you can stop worrying and enjoy your day no matter what the sky does.

Rain is not the enemy on film

Here is something couples do not expect me to say: a bit of rain can be beautiful on camera. Soft grey light is actually flattering, umbrellas make for gorgeous shots, and there is something intimate about a couple stealing a kiss under cover. I have filmed rainy weddings that couples ended up loving more than they ever expected.

Plan for light and the little country things

  • Golden hour. The hour before sunset is the best light of the day. If you can, sneak out for a few minutes of portraits then.
  • Avoid harsh midday sun for the ceremony if you can. Later afternoon is kinder to everyone.
  • Bugs and heat. A summer evening in the country brings bugs at dusk. A little planning, and having your key moments before then, helps.
  • Wind. Open fields can be windy, which affects sound, so it is worth mentioning your setup to your videographer.

Whatever your day brings, I adapt to it. My job is to make sure your film feels like the day, sunshine, rain, or a bit of both.
